slides.title: Dispatch Copilot: launch, packaging and price

claims.claim: Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro plan at $12 more per seat, not as a $149 add-on, and plan on about $2.9M of ARR, not $8M
Copilot is worth launching: it improved beta productivity and renewals, and Routewise has made AI part of the buying decision
evidence: Beta jobs per dispatcher-hour rose 11%, against 2% for matched accounts
Our win rate against Routewise fell from 44% to 37% after it bundled AI

claims.claim: The prize is a third of what the plan assumes: real purchases point to about $2.5M of add-on ARR, not $8M
evidence: Only 14% of beta accounts paid, against 46% survey intent
Win-back from Routewise is worth at most $0.6M a year

claims.claim: Package Copilot in Pro at $12 more per seat with a fair-use allowance, rather than as a flat $149 add-on
evidence: Pro closes the NRR gap if 26% move up; our 2023 tier drew 33%
A fair-use allowance keeps gross margin above the 75% floor

claims.claim: The real cost is the two-quarter mobile delay, yet launching still adds about $2.4M of net ARR under five conditions

slides.title: Copilot lifted productivity and renewals in the beta, but volunteer accounts likely overstate both gains

claims.claim: Beta dispatchers scheduled more jobs per hour than matched accounts did
evidence: +9 pp
Change in jobs per dispatcher-hour: Beta accounts 0.11; Matched non-beta accounts 0.02

claims.claim: Beta accounts also renewed more often than matched accounts
evidence: +4 pp
90-day renewal rate: Beta accounts 0.97; Matched non-beta accounts 0.93

claims.claim: Treat both gains as a ceiling: the 240 beta accounts volunteered and average 8.1 seats, against 6.2 across all accounts
evidence: Beta dispatchers also reported saving 4.1 hours a week (self-reported, no comparison group)

slides.title: Our win rate against Routewise fell from 44% to 37% once it bundled AI, making AI part of the buying decision

claims.claim: Our win rate against Routewise fell from 44% to 37% once it bundled AI
evidence: Q3 2026: the fall came in the quarter Routewise put AI scheduling into its Pro plan (September)

claims.claim: AI now shows up in how we lose deals
evidence: Loss notes: 31% of Q3 lost deals mention AI features, so prospects now ask for it

claims.claim: Caveat: Routewise also offered 20% off the first year in Q3, so price explains part of the fall
Without Copilot we face Routewise's bundled AI in about 60% of our 2,600 qualified opportunities a year

slides.title: Only 14% of beta accounts bought Copilot when asked to pay, against 46% who said they would in the survey

evidence: Survey: likely or very likely to buy at $149 0.46; Paywall test: bought at $149 0.14
3.3x times as many said they would buy as actually bought
October 2026 survey (n = 610) and beta paywall test (n = 120)

claims.claim: Survey: only 6% of admins replied, and respondents average 9.4 seats against 6.2 for all accounts
evidence: sent to all 9,800 account admins

claims.claim: Paywall test: 17 of 120 accounts paid after the free period; they are volunteers, larger and more active than the base, so even this rate is a ceiling
Planning rule: size Copilot on what accounts paid, not on what admins said

slides.title: Sized on actual purchases, the add-on would bring about $2.5M of first-year ARR, under a third of the $8M forecast

claims.claim: Sized on actual purchases, the add-on would bring about $2.5M of first-year ARR, under a third of the $8M forecast
evidence: First-year new ARR: CPO forecast, survey-based 8; Based on paywall purchases 2.453
9,800 customer accounts × 14% bought in the paywall test × $1,788 add-on revenue per account a year ($149 × 12) = $2.5M first-year ARR, a ceiling
Purchase basis: the same formula at the 14% seen in the paywall test, about 1,372 paying accounts

claims.claim: The forecast assumes every 'likely' admin buys
evidence: CPO forecast: applies the survey's 46% to all 9,800 accounts at $1,788 a year each

claims.claim: Still optimistic: the test ran on volunteers after 12 free weeks, so the base is likely to convert at a lower rate

slides.title: The sales memo's claim is three times the whole fall in wins; win-back is worth at most about $0.6M of ARR

claims.claim: The sales memo's claim is three times the whole fall in wins
evidence: 328 deals a year the memo expects Copilot to recover (A third of 983 deals lost to Routewise a year)
109 fewer wins a year since Routewise bundled AI
Memo: "31% of our lost deals cite AI, so Copilot would recover about a third of the deals we lose to Routewise"
Reads 31% of loss notes mentioning AI as AI causing the loss
Loss notes cover all lost deals, not only Routewise ones

claims.claim: win-back is worth at most about $0.6M of ARR
evidence: 1,560 opportunities a year where Routewise competes (2,600 × 60%) × 7 pp fall in win rate × $5,878 ARR of a new 6.2-seat Core account = $0.6M new ARR a year at stake, a ceiling
Part of the fall likely reflects Routewise's 20% first-year discount
Winning back more would beat our own pre-AI win rate

claims.claim: Worth defending, but not the main reason to launch
evidence: About a fifth of Pro's first-year ARR

slides.title: A flat add-on fee draws the heaviest users: buyers averaged 6,800 requests a month, 3.6 times the median account

claims.claim: A flat add-on fee draws the heaviest users: buyers averaged 6,800 requests a month, 3.6 times the median account
evidence: Requests per month: Top 10% of beta accounts, mean 14500; Accounts that bought at $149 6800; Beta account, mean 3600; Beta account, median 1900
3.6x times the median account's use among accounts that paid

claims.claim: Top 10%: these accounts generate 58% of all requests, so a few accounts drive most of the cost
Buyers: each costs $61.20 a month in inference at $0.009 a request, 41% of the $149 fee
evidence: Inference cost of $0.009 per request is fixed under the current provider contract through December 2027

claims.claim: Pricing lesson: a flat fee is cheapest for the heaviest users; a seat price grows with the account

slides.title: Pro is the better package because it grows with account size, reaches a broader base and matches Routewise

claims.claim: Pro's price rises with seats, and so does use
evidence: List price per month: $149 add-on per account vs $12 Pro per seat

claims.claim: Pro's precedent covers the whole base, not volunteers
evidence: Uptake seen so far: add-on 14% (paywall test); Pro 33% (2023 tier launch)

claims.claim: The add-on attracts the heaviest users
evidence: Inference cost per paying account a month: add-on $61.2; Pro $32.4
Pro inference cost assumes Pro accounts use Copilot like the mean beta account; add-on cost uses the paywall buyers' 6,800 requests a month

claims.claim: Matches the offer we now lose to
evidence: Add-on: AI sold separately, at extra cost; Pro: AI included in the plan, as at Routewise
Routewise has included AI scheduling in its Pro plan since September 2026

claims.claim: Pro's risk has a fix: a fair-use allowance
evidence: Main risk: add-on — Demand rests on a test of volunteers; Pro — Heavy users inside a seat price

slides.title: Pro would close the NRR gap on its own if 26% of accounts move up, fewer than our 2023 tier attracted

claims.claim: Pro would close the NRR gap on its own if 26% of accounts move up
evidence: $2.3M extra net ARR a year to lift NRR by 4 percentage points on $57.6M ÷ $893 Pro premium per account a year ($12 × 6.2 seats × 12) ÷ 9,800 customer accounts = 26% of accounts must move to Pro
lift NRR from 101% to 105%

claims.claim: The threshold is a realistic gate, not a stretch
evidence: Our 2023 higher tier drew 33% of accounts within a year; at that rate Pro adds about $2.9M of ARR

claims.claim: Churn, contraction and other expansion stay at today's level, so Pro carries the whole gap
Accounts that move have the average 6.2 seats; larger movers would lower the threshold
The 2023 tier did not include AI, so Copilot's own pull on uptake is still untested

slides.title: Pro needs a fair-use allowance: a top-10% account would cost $130.50 a month to serve, against $74.40 of Pro revenue

claims.claim: Pro needs a fair-use allowance: a top-10% account would cost $130.50 a month to serve, against $74.40 of Pro revenue
evidence: Inference cost per month: Top-10% beta account 130.5; Account that bought at $149 61.2; 6.2-seat account at the allowance 37.2; Beta account, mean 32.4; Pro premium, 6.2-seat account 74.4

claims.claim: With the allowance, margin stays above the 75% floor
evidence: Pro at beta-average use: 76%, Copilot cost $1.86M a year on $2.89M of Pro ARR
Every Pro account used like a buyer, no allowance: 74.1%, Copilot cost rises to $2.98M a year
Same heavy use, capped at the allowance: 75.7%, Copilot cost capped at $2.04M a year
Margins: today's $44.9M gross profit (78% of $57.6M) plus Pro ARR less Copilot cost, over total revenue; the $0.6M platform cost is counted as cost of revenue

claims.claim: Allowance of 667 requests per seat a month keeps inference at half the $12 seat price, above the beta average of 444 per seat; use above it is sold as request packs

slides.title: Mobile reliability drives 4.5 times as much churn as missing AI, which makes the rewrite delay Copilot's real cost

claims.claim: Mobile reliability drives 4.5 times as much churn as missing AI
evidence: Share of churned accounts, 2026 (n = 1,190): Mobile app reliability 0.27; Price 0.22; Missing integrations 0.15; Went out of business / sold 0.14; Switched for AI features 0.06; Other 0.16
4.5x times as many accounts left over the mobile app as left for AI

claims.claim: Mobile app: also the top request, ranked first by 38% of surveyed customers against 19% for AI scheduling
AI features: a small churn driver, so Copilot is a growth and win-rate lever more than a retention fix
Price: the second reason, which argues for a tier customers choose over a price rise for all
Launch Copilot, but treat the mobile rewrite's new date as fixed

slides.title: Even charging the mobile delay in full, launching in Pro adds about $2.4M of net ARR in the first year

claims.claim: Even charging the mobile delay in full, launching in Pro adds about $2.4M of net ARR in the first year
evidence: $2.9M Pro ARR if 33% of accounts move, as with the 2023 tier + $0.6M new-logo win-back at most − $1.1M mobile-driven churn during the two-quarter delay, at most = $2.4M net new ARR in the first year

claims.claim: Both risks are counted at their ceiling
evidence: Pro ARR: 9,800 accounts × 33% × $893 premium a year, with movers at the average 6.2 seats
Mobile delay: $57.6M ARR × 14% churn × 27% citing mobile × half a year, as if the rewrite would end all mobile churn

claims.claim: Not netted: the one-time $1.47M of engineering (14 of our 60 engineers for two quarters at $210,000 a year)
The mobile delay could cost up to 38% of Pro's first-year ARR, so the rewrite's new date must hold
The delay is worth accepting only with the rewrite's new date and team locked before launch

slides.title: Five conditions turn the launch from a bet into a managed test

claims.claim: Sell Copilot only inside a new Pro plan; drop the add-on
evidence: $12 more per seat a month than Core

claims.claim: Cap use per seat; sell request packs above the cap
evidence: 667 requests per seat a month

claims.claim: Review Pro uptake after two quarters
evidence: 105% NRR target for 2028

claims.claim: Test productivity on non-volunteers
evidence: 240 beta accounts, all volunteers

claims.claim: Keep the mobile rewrite team and date fixed
evidence: 27% of churn is over mobile reliability

claims.claim: Inference is fixed at $0.009 a request through December 2027; the provider's list prices fell 35% over the past 12 months, so reprice before renewal

normalized.recommendation: Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro plan at $12 more per seat, not as a $149 add-on, and plan on about $2.9M of ARR, not $8M; package it with a fair-use allowance (667 requests per seat a month, request packs above the cap), under five conditions: sell only inside Pro and drop the add-on, cap use per seat, review Pro uptake after two quarters, test productivity on non-volunteers, and keep the mobile rewrite team and date fixed.

alternatives_considered.option: $149 flat add-on per account per month
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: real purchases point to about $2.5M of add-on ARR, not $8M; a flat add-on fee draws the heaviest users (buyers averaged 6,800 requests a month, $61.2 inference cost per paying account); demand rests on a test of volunteers; AI sold separately unlike Routewise. 'retire the $149 add-on plan'.

alternatives_considered.option: Pro plan at $12 more per seat with fair-use allowance
alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen: grows with account size, reaches a broader base and matches Routewise; closes NRR gap if 26% move up vs 33% for 2023 tier; fair-use allowance keeps gross margin above the 75% floor.
Rejected: every Pro account used like a buyer, no allowance, margin falls to 74.1%, below the 75% floor; a top-10% account would cost $130.50 a month against $74.40 of Pro revenue.
Rejected as sizing basis: assumes every 'likely' admin buys; 'size Copilot on what accounts paid, not on what admins said'.
Price as second churn reason 'argues for a tier customers choose over a price rise for all'.
